outline:
Course Outline and Objectives
This course provides an introduction to the principles of information technologies and programming coding skills that can be used in interaction design element of the multimedia production process. Course activities are focused on programming coding skills training and the descriptions, contents, principles and applications of the changes to the digital technologies of interaction design and their future trends. This course encourages students to critically engage with interdisciplinary approaches to information technologies and interaction design in a context of peer support and feedback, in order to forge their own unique personal skills. These skills are then applied to a real-world design project in which students work with a project, with advice and input from industry professionals.
By the time students have successfully completed this course, they should be able to:
? Use information technologies and programming coding skills to define a digital interaction design experience, and its differences and similarities with other types of experiences
? Think critically about how people experience digital interaction design and media products and how such experiences can be designed and implement using programming tools.
? Develop and articulate a personal experiences and programming coding skills of digital interaction design
? Refine personal skills of digital interaction design through application of personal skills to the design of a digital project and evaluation of that project
? Compare and contrast existing digital technologies and programming skills of interaction design
Class Sessions and learning strategies
This course includes face-to-face classes and e-tivities throughout the semester, constituted by weekly activities that include lectures, moderated round-table discussion and presentation of assigned reading papers. You will gain most from the classes if you prepare in advance and participate in the discussions. The NTTU online e-Learning system （網路學園） will be used in this course for discussions, activities, assessment progression and submission, a question and answer forum and course announcements. More details of the group and round-table discussions will be given in classes and in the NTTU online e-Learning system. As a student in this course you are expected to attend and participate in all classes, actively contribute to online discussions, and complete your assignments and term project by their due dates. This course is 3 credit points. This means that you should be spending an average of 6-9 hours per week on this subject throughout the semester.
